The decision in plain English

You do not need to become a developer. You need to turn “maybe a double lot” into a documented asset that a buyer, lender, broker, title company and City can understand. Once that proof exists, there are three realistic money exits:

  1. Sell the house-side parcel and keep the empty lot — best fit if the split is clean and house-sale proceeds can pay the mortgage in full.
  2. Sell the whole property with the split story proven — fastest low-capital fallback; let a builder finish the subdivision.
  3. Sell the vacant lot and keep the house — only if the lender confirms the sale will truly fix monthly affordability through payoff, recast or refinance.

Hard stop

If survey + City say the two-lot route is not clean, stop spending. Market 1011 as one R-12 property with two-dwelling potential instead of chasing a costly exception.

1Capture cooperationAsk for the front-only gift. If 1007 says yes, sign cooperation + survey access that day.

3Re-price the exitsGet current BPOs for whole, house-side, vacant-side and whole-with-proven-feasibility.
4Choose the exitUse the least expensive path that actually solves the mortgage problem while preserving equity.

Strategy04 / 23
Compare the exits
Which option actually solves your problem?

The objective is not the biggest theoretical project. It is the best combination of debt relief, cash, speed, retained equity and low out-of-pocket risk.

1

Split → sell the house-side parcel → keep the buildable lot

AV preferred owner outcome if the split is proven and the house-side sale can pay the mortgage in full. The owner moves, debt goes to zero, and you retain an empty buildable parcel that can be sold later, held, or used as collateral only if desired.

2

Prove split feasibility → sell the whole property to a builder/developer

Best low-cash fallback. You monetize certainty without paying for final plat, infrastructure or construction. This can also be structured as a buyer-funded entitlement closing or option if counsel/title approve.

3

Split → sell the vacant half → keep the house

This matches your initial instinct and can work — but the lender mechanics decide whether it solves affordability. If the lot sale simply pays down principal and the loan is not recast/refinanced, the scheduled monthly payment may remain largely unchanged.

4

Split → sell both parcels separately

Potentially the highest gross liquidity without building. More time, more transactional work, and more exposure to two separate marketing periods.

5

Sell 1011 whole today / as-is

Fastest conceptual path, but likely leaves the split premium to the next owner. It should still be priced and kept as the emergency exit benchmark, even if it is not the preferred plan.

6

Build a second home / ADU / duplex

Strong long-term development rights, poor fit for your current capital constraint. The 1911 house also adds demolition-review process to a teardown strategy.

Strategy05 / 23
The key strategic debate
Why selling the house first may be better than selling the empty half first
▶
Hear the money-strategy briefingWhy house-side-first currently leads and when vacant-lot-first could still work.

Sell vacant lot first

  • Requires lender partial release because the mortgage/deed of trust will generally still affect both new parcels until released.
  • Lender may demand much or all of the net lot proceeds as principal paydown.
  • Principal paydown ≠ lower payment. The lender may need to approve a recast or the owner may need a refinance.
  • Owner still owns and must maintain the 1911 house.
  • Vacant land can have a smaller buyer pool and longer marketing time.

Sell house side first

  • If net house-sale proceeds exceed the mortgage payoff, the loan can be retired completely at closing.
  • Once the debt is paid and title handles releases correctly, the retained lot can be owned free and clear.
  • Owner gets an immediate clean break from the monthly mortgage.
  • Potential for cash at closing plus retained lot equity.
  • Owner must move, which aligns with the desired exit within a year.

Illustrative—not appraised—$300k / $350k / $400k debt comparison

Example only: house-side gross $500k; vacant lot gross $299k; whole-property benchmark $584.7k; 6% blended sale friction; $20k entitlement/diligence budget. Actual values and fees must be replaced with BPO/title/lender quotes.

DebtHouse first: cash after debt & $20k diligenceAsset keptLot first: approx. debt remaining after lot net & diligence*Whole as-is: approx. cash
$300k~$150kVacant lot (~$299k planning input)~$39k~$250k
$350k~$100kVacant lot (~$299k planning input)~$89k~$200k
$400k~$50kVacant lot (~$299k planning input)~$139k~$150k

*Assumes all available lot-sale proceeds are applied to debt. This does not mean the monthly payment falls proportionally; ask the lender about recast/refinance terms and partial-release conditions before selecting this route.

Why this matters: whole-as-is may produce more immediate cash than house-first in some debt cases, but it leaves the owner with no retained asset. House-first is the hybrid: cash + zero mortgage + land retained, if the split and pricing both work.

Your first time doing a land / title transaction
Exactly what you do, in order

You do not need to know surveying, subdivision law or title work. Your job is to hire the right people, ask the right questions, keep the process moving, and stop spending when a decision gate turns red.

▶
Hear your first-week briefingA first-time-owner sequence for the neighbor agreement, survey, title and City questions.
Golden rule: never pay for the next stage until the current stage has answered the question that justifies it.

Before you talk to 1007

Print / save two copiesBring the same-day Conditional Boundary Gift & Active-Sale Cooperation Agreement, survey-access authorization, and listing-broker notice.
Have photo ID availableIf you decide to use a notary that day, each signer should have acceptable government ID.
Know your private ceilingIf the gift is declined, decide before the call whether you authorize any paid fallback and the maximum same-call amount. Do not invent a number under pressure.
Have a phone scanner readyUse your phone to photograph/scan every signed page before anyone leaves. Send each side a complete copy.
Line up 2–3 surveyorsYou do not need to hire one before the conversation, but have names/phones ready so a “yes” can become a rush order the same day.
Identify title / escrowKnow which local title company you will call to open a limited BLA/title file on both parcels.

Your step-by-step path

Ask 1007 friend-to-friend

Use the short script on the Boundary page. Ask for the small front portion as a gift, conditioned on survey and City review showing it does not create a problem for 1007.

Your result: yes, no, or “maybe / need to think.” Do not debate.

If they say YES, capture it before you leave

Go directly to the 1007 Said YES page. Fill in names/date/time, sign the same-day conditional agreement, sign survey access, scan copies, and notify the listing agent. If a notary is available, acknowledge signatures. Do not sign an improvised or blank deed.

Your result: dated written consent + permission to start diligence.

Order the survey

Call the selected surveyor and say this is a rush boundary / improvement + BLA feasibility assignment. Email the exact scope from this report. Ask for price, field date, expected preliminary exhibit date, and whether they will prepare the later Record of Survey / deed exhibit.

Do not order: house plans, engineering design, architecture or final subdivision work yet.

Open title on BOTH parcels

Tell title: “I own 1011 and I am evaluating a small boundary-line gift from 1007. Please confirm vesting, legal descriptions, deeds of trust, liens, easements and whether 1007 needs a lender partial release.” Give them both APNs.

Your result: you know who actually must sign and whether a bank controls the strip.

Get the surveyor's preliminary exhibit

Do not wait for a polished final plat. First you want exact B Street frontage, existing/proposed boundary, 1007 garage/wall distances, your house footprint, access/easements/utilities, and a conceptual future 50/50 split.

Stop / redesign if: the front line cannot become a defensible 100.00 feet, the line creates a new 1007 setback problem, or your existing house makes the future split unworkable.

Take the exhibit to CDA Planning / Engineering

Ask the two decisive questions in writing: (1) does the City recognize 100.00 feet of frontage after the front-only jog; and (2) can the future southern lot have 50 feet at B Street but narrow to about 49 feet behind the first ~30 feet while still being eligible for the intended subdivision path?

Your result: written City direction before you spend on entitlement.

Only then finalize the BLA transaction

If survey, City, title and any lender release are green, have Idaho counsel/title review the binding documents. The surveyor creates the actual metes-and-bounds description. Then the City BLA, Record of Survey and warranty deed can move toward approval/recording.

Re-price the property before deciding how far to subdivide

Ask at least two brokers to price: today’s whole property; whole property with documented BLA/split feasibility; house-side future parcel; and vacant future parcel. Compare the premium to the remaining short-plat/final-plat cost and time.

Call your mortgage servicer with exact questions

Get written partial-release, payoff and recast rules. If the house-side sale can fully pay off the mortgage and release the retained lot, that remains the preferred clean-exit model. Do not assume a vacant-lot sale will lower your scheduled payment.

Choose the least expensive exit that solves your problem

If the market will pay you for proven feasibility, you may stop before final plat. If recorded lots add enough value to justify the next expense, proceed. Your goal is financial freedom, not finishing every possible development step.

Highest-leverage low-cost move
The 1007 front-30-foot boundary strategy

Your memory of a “1 ft” issue is supported by the parcel/legal reconstruction. The preferred solution is not a full-depth strip: target the street frontage and stay away from the 1007 garage.

Active-sale reality: current web results show 1007 actively listed around $835,000 as of Sep. 15, 2026, with a recent price cut. If your friend says yes, go immediately to the 1007 Said YES page and capture it in writing.

Friend-first proposal

“We found an old county record showing a one-foot piece from 1011 was combined with your parcel years ago. We’re checking whether correcting only the front ~30 feet would help clean up our frontage. Would you be open to gifting that tiny front piece back if a survey and the City confirm it doesn’t create any problem for your property? We’d structure it so the line goes back to where it is now before your garage.”

Do not tell 1007 that you are under financial pressure. Be truthful that the adjustment may improve frontage / future options. Do not promise subdivision approval.

City BLA rules
≤2 turns

City code permits no more than two deflection points on the adjusted line, requires compliant resulting lots, a surveyor-prepared Record of Survey, and a warranty deed with metes-and-bounds.

If the gift is declined — same-call paid fallback

Step 1 — keep it friendly and make them name the number.
“I understand. If a gift doesn’t work for you, is there a number that would make the small front piece worth doing, assuming the survey and City confirm it doesn’t hurt your property?”
Step 2 — do not bid against yourself.

If they ask you to make the first offer, only use a number you have decided in advance. Prior owner-side planning suggested a low anchor around $2,500 and a same-call ceiling around $5,000 only only if you decide that ceiling before the conversation. Anything above that ceiling should stop the conversation until you decide privately.

Step 3 — document it correctly.

The instant money or other consideration is agreed, stop calling the conveyance a gift. The gift deed/agreement must be replaced or amended into a paid BLA conveyance through Idaho counsel/title.

Negotiation principle: do not pay based on the value the 30 square feet may unlock for 1011. Negotiate based on the practical impact and market value to 1007, while ensuring 1007 is free to obtain independent advice.

City / survey requirements to protect both properties

  • Exact B Street frontage before and after.
  • Every 1007 structure wall distance to current and proposed line.
  • 1011 house footprint against the future split line and required yard.
  • Existing sewer/water services and access.
  • Title, easements, liens and any lender partial release required at 1007.
  • City confirmation that the irregular future southern lot geometry is acceptable.

Sign the right document at the right time
Your document kit — what each paper is for
▤
Document kitPrint only this document/section without printing the full Powerhouse.
Same day after YES

Conditional Boundary Gift & Active-Sale Cooperation Agreement

Captures 1007's present gift intent, survey/title/City cooperation, active-listing notice obligations, diligence window and the plan if a buyer appears before the BLA records.

It is not the deed. Optional same-day notarization authenticates signatures but does not transfer the land.

Same day after YES

Survey Access Authorization

Lets your licensed surveyor enter reasonable exterior portions of 1007 to locate the shared line and nearby structures. This is important because the 1007 garage is the reason the front-only line was developed.

Same day / next day

Listing Broker Notice & Coordination Authorization

Lets the active listing continue while alerting the broker that a minor BLA is pending. If an offer arrives, title/broker/buyer can coordinate rather than accidentally close over the issue.

Only if buyer appears first

Buyer Assumption of Pending BLA

If 1007 goes under contract before the BLA records, this is the bridge document for the incoming buyer to acknowledge the pending boundary work and agree to continue reasonable cooperation after closing, subject to buyer/lender/title review.

After survey + title + City feasibility

Binding Conditional BLA / Gift Agreement

Use Idaho counsel/title review before relying on it. Conditions should include final survey geometry, no new nonconformity, City approval, acceptable title, required lender release and your approved budget.

Do not sign early

Gift Warranty Deed + survey Exhibit A

This is the actual conveyance document. It should contain the surveyor-prepared metes-and-bounds description accepted by City/title, and be coordinated with the approved Record of Survey and any required lender release.

If gift becomes paid

Paid Frontage Term Sheet + Conditional BLA Purchase Agreement

The moment 1007 requires compensation, stop using the gift agreement/deed as the operative documents. Capture the exact fixed price in the paid term sheet, keep the survey/City/title/lender/no-harm conditions, and normally route payment through title/escrow when the approved BLA can record.

If a notary is there: use the optional acknowledgments on the cooperation agreement if both sides are comfortable. That captures who signed and when. The actual warranty deed still waits for the surveyor’s legal description and the City/title/lender path.
TermWhat it means for you
Gift intent1007 states the present intent to gift the final City-approved transfer area; no land purchase price unless you later amend the deal in writing.
Concept area onlyAbout 1 foot south at B Street for about 30 feet, then back to the existing line before the garage. The licensed survey controls the final shape and legal description.
Immediate access / cooperation1007 permits reasonable exterior survey access and agrees to cooperate with survey, title, City and lender questions that do not impose an unapproved cost on them.
Active listing protection1007 may keep marketing the home, but the listing agent should be notified. If 1007 accepts an offer before the BLA records, you should receive prompt notice—our working draft uses one business day.
Buyer appears before recordingTry to complete the BLA before 1007 closes, or have the incoming buyer sign an assumption/cooperation document so the process does not die at closing.
Diligence windowThe working draft uses 15 business days for the initial survey/title/City push, with a limited extension for third-party delays and a 45-day long-stop unless everyone agrees otherwise.
Conditions before deedNo final conveyance until survey geometry, City approval, title, no new nonconformity, any required lender release, and your approved cost budget are acceptable.
Reliance costsThe working draft lets the parties choose either “each side bears its own costs” or a capped reimbursement of your documented third-party costs if 1007 voluntarily defeats the process after you rely on the signed agreement. Idaho counsel should finalize this clause.
No recording of the cooperation agreementDo not cloud title by recording the working cooperation contract unless Idaho counsel/title specifically directs otherwise.
No standalone sliverThe ~30-sf concept area must merge into 1011 through the approved BLA; it is not a tiny independent parcel.
No subdivision promiseThe agreement captures cooperation. It does not promise that CDA will later approve two lots.

Who you call — and what each person actually does

A first-time land transaction feels complicated because several specialists touch one small boundary. You do not need one person who “does everything.” You need each professional to answer one narrow question.

AeroVista does not act for 1007 and does not sign for you. AV organizes the research, strategy, scripts, working drafts and decision gates; you hire and direct the surveyor, title/escrow, attorney, broker, lender and CPA.

MASTER COMPLETE · section 12 of 23
Financial / exit13 / 23
The part that can make or break the exit
Mortgage, title & tax mechanics

Mortgage reality after subdivision

Creating two legal lots does not automatically split the loan. The existing deed of trust can continue to encumber the property created from the parent parcel until the lender releases or reconveys it.

If selling the vacant lot first

Get the lender's written partial-release terms before listing. The lender may require most or all net proceeds to reduce principal. Then ask whether the remaining loan will be recast; otherwise the monthly payment may not fall.

If selling the house side first

If the sale nets enough to pay the loan in full, escrow can obtain payoff/reconveyance and the retained vacant lot can emerge debt-free, subject to title coordination.

Five lender questions

  1. After a two-lot subdivision, what is required for a partial release of one lot?
  2. How much of a lot sale must be applied to principal?
  3. Will the lender recast the remaining loan after a large principal payment, and what are the eligibility/fees?
  4. If the house-side sale pays the loan in full, will escrow receive a payoff/reconveyance sufficient to clear the retained lot?
  5. Are there appraisal, seasoning, LTV, modification or consent requirements triggered by the BLA or subdivision?

Tax timing can influence which parcel sells first

IRS Publication 523 says a taxpayer may be able to include the sale of vacant land adjacent to the home as part of the home sale if the land was owned/used as part of the home, the land sale and home sale occur within two years of each other, and both sales satisfy the applicable eligibility rules. The home-sale exclusion is generally up to $250,000 of gain for a qualifying single filer or $500,000 for qualifying married filing jointly. This is a CPA question, not a reason to improvise the closing order.

Roommates / Airbnb note

Short-term or roommate income may be the bridge that buys enough time to complete survey and City work. But rental/business use and depreciation can affect tax treatment. If depreciation was claimed or allowable, some gain may not be excludable. Give the CPA the tax returns and rental history before finalizing sale sequencing.

Title note

The 1007 → 1011 boundary transfer also needs title review. If 1007 is mortgaged, its lender may need to release the transfer area. Do not record around a deed of trust, easement or lien problem.

Do the cheapest decisive work first
Your 12-month roadmap

The plan is designed so you can stop early and still have something valuable to sell.

Where you are now: Stage 1 — secure 1007 cooperation and immediately launch survey/title. Do not treat this as a subdivision project until the preliminary survey and written City answers justify Stage 2 spending.
Days 0–3

Neighbor conversation + same-day capture + rush orders

Make the gift request to 1007. If yes, sign the same-day cooperation agreement and survey access immediately, notify the listing agent, and order rush survey/title work the same day or next business morning. Also call your mortgage servicer about partial release / recast / payoff mechanics.

Days 3–14

Survey + City written feasibility

Field survey and preliminary BLA exhibit. Ask the two frontage/irregular-lot questions in writing. If the answer is bad, stop and pivot.

Weeks 2–6

BLA decision

If green, finalize the gift or paid BLA documents, satisfy title/lender issues and file the BLA. Simultaneously order broker opinions for three products: house-side, vacant lot, and whole property with documented split potential.

Months 2–4

Choose sale level

Decision point: sell the whole property with documented feasibility, or proceed into preliminary short plat because the incremental premium justifies it.

Months 3–7

Short plat / final work if justified

Complete only the entitlement level the economics support. Avoid construction. Keep your carrying cost stable with existing income where lawful and practical.

Months 4–10

Market selected parcel(s)

Preferred case: list the house-side parcel, coordinate full mortgage payoff, retain the lot. Alternative: sell both or sell whole.

By month 12

Exit

You are out of the unaffordable mortgage. You either retain a debt-free buildable lot or converts the entire asset to cash.

Runway rule: if your cash / roommate / Airbnb bridge cannot reliably carry the property through the next decision gate, do not chase the final plat. Sell the proven opportunity sooner.

Financial / exit16 / 23
What to say, what to ask, what not to forget
Your action cheat wiki

Call the lender

“I am evaluating a two-lot subdivision of my existing mortgaged property. Before I spend money, I need your written process for partial release of one resulting parcel, required principal curtailment, whether the remaining loan can be recast, and how a full payoff from the sale of one parcel would release the other parcel.”

Call the surveyor

“The goal is not a generic boundary survey. I need to prove exact B Street frontage, protect the 1007 garage setback, test a 1-foot by roughly 30-foot front BLA with no more than two deflections, and show whether 1011 can later support two 50-foot-frontage R-12 lots with the existing house.”

Ask the City

“If the BLA gives 1011 a surveyed 100.00-foot front lot line for the first ~30 feet and the south boundary then jogs one foot north, does the City recognize 100.00 feet of R-12 frontage? Can the parcel then be short-platted into two lots with 50 feet of street frontage each if one narrows to roughly 49 feet behind the front segment?”

Ask the broker / BPO

“Price three different products, not one: (1) 1011 today, (2) the existing house on a future ~50-foot lot after split, and (3) the future vacant ~50-foot lot. Then price the whole property again assuming written City feasibility but before final plat.”

Do / don't

DoDon't
Spend money only on questions that change the exit decision.Do not demolish, build, or commission expensive architecture now.
Keep your financial pressure confidential in neighbor and buyer negotiation.Do not lie about the purpose or deny that the boundary may have development value.
Get lender release/recast terms in writing before selling only one parcel.Do not assume selling the lot will lower the monthly mortgage.
Get City treatment in writing before advertising two legal lots.Do not treat GIS lines or our 99×117.5 reconstruction as survey evidence.
Use title/escrow and Idaho counsel for the BLA/deed.Do not record a 30-sf standalone parcel or a hand-drawn legal description.

Glossary

BLA
Boundary Line Adjustment: moves a shared boundary but does not create a new lot.
Short plat
City subdivision path for four or fewer lots with no new public right-of-way, provided frontage standards are met.
Partial release
Lender releases one parcel/strip from the mortgage lien while the loan continues on remaining collateral.
Recast
Lender re-amortizes the remaining principal after a large payment, potentially reducing the scheduled payment without a full refinance.
Payoff / reconveyance
Loan is paid in full and the deed of trust lien is released.
Record of Survey
Surveyor-prepared recorded document showing the approved boundary geometry.
BPO
Broker Price Opinion. Use multiple BPOs to price each exit product before choosing.
Section 121
Federal principal-residence gain exclusion rules. Vacant adjacent land has special timing rules.

Cross-conversation sweep · what was still missing

Deep diligence, hidden constraints & fallback value

This page pulls in the material items that were present in the earlier parcel-detail, subdivision, LotScope, gift-document and negotiation conversations but were not fully carried into the first powerhouse version. It separates what is now strongly supported from what still has to be proved by survey, title, City records or the mortgage servicer.

1. The legal-description story is stronger than “double lot”

ParcelWorking legal description from prior parcel researchWhy it matters
1011 · C3510003001AFOREST HEIGHTS, LT 1, LT 2 EX S 1 FT BLK 3 1450N04WIt expressly excludes the south 1 foot of original Lot 2.
1007 · C3510003003AFOREST HEIGHTS, S 1 FT OF LT 2, LT 3, N2 OF LT 4 BLOCK 3 1450N04WIt contains the complementary south 1 foot of Lot 2. The current 1007 MLS/public record also reports 8,930 sf.

The 99' × 117.5' reconstruction is unusually coherent with the reported 11,633 sf area, but it is still analytical reconstruction — not survey control. The original Forest Heights plat is indexed as Book B, Page 82. We have the plat locator; we still need the actual recorded scan and the 2012 instrument that moved/combined the one-foot piece.

Record pull still needed
3 items

Original Forest Heights plat (Book B/Page 82), the 2012 recorded instrument affecting the one-foot strip, and a current title commitment / Schedule B for both 1011 and 1007.

2. Alley / rear access is still a high-leverage unknown

Evidence that an alley system exists in this block pattern

City wastewater construction records include sanitary-sewer work identified as the “ALLEY BETWEEN A & B ST.” in this neighborhood. That supports the old-block/alley theory.

It does not prove that 1011 has a currently unvacated legal rear-access right. The recorded plat, title exceptions and any vacation instruments control.

Open City alley/sewer plan set

Why alley status changes the site

R-12 normally requires a 5-foot interior side yard, but prior code review found that when there is no alley or other legal rear access, at least one side yard must be 10 feet. Confirmed rear access can therefore materially change the future house-side envelope, driveway strategy and whether the existing 1911 house can remain after a split.

Put “unvacated legal alley/rear access” in the title/survey scope — do not settle for “I can see an alley on the aerial.”

3. Utilities can turn a clean paper split into an expensive one

The City says its Wastewater staff maintains a GIS of the collection system and regularly updates sanitary-sewer lateral locations from CCTV footage. City directory guidance lists sewer information at 208-769-2281 and sewer-stub locates through 811. Existing public sources report 1011 has public water and public sewer, but that is not enough for a two-parcel closing.

Ask forReason
Existing sewer lateral location, size, connection point and conditionWe need to know whether each future lot can have a lawful independent service without crossing the other lot.
Water meter/service size and main locationA second legal parcel may require an independent tap/meter or capacity work.
Utility easements / private-crossing rightsA split that leaves one parcel dependent on unrecorded utilities across the other is not sale-ready.
Required frontage improvements / sidewalk / approach workThese can become a major cost swing at final-plat stage.

For your low-cash exit strategy, utility certainty is worth buying; utility construction is usually not. If a buyer can fund the expensive part, sell them the proven entitlement package instead.

Official contacts

Sewer info: 208-769-2281
Sewer stub locate: 811
Engineering / subdivisions: 208-769-2235
Planning / setbacks: 208-769-2274

Open City directory

4. Permit history is not closed

Do not mistake “nothing found in Google” for “no permit history.” The City has a direct address-based permit-search system. The house dates to 1911, so some history may predate digital records; the reported 1985 renovation is not, by itself, proof of permitting.

Pull by address / APN

Search building, mechanical, plumbing, remodel, reroof, demolition and accessory-structure records. Pay special attention to the existing storage/garage-type improvements and any old conversion work that a buyer or appraiser could flag.

Open CDA permit search

Why this matters to the exit

An unpermitted addition or utility condition can reduce appraisal value, complicate title/insurance, or create a late buyer objection. Finding it during cheap diligence is much better than finding it during escrow.

5. The split is not the only real entitlement

Important fallback: current R-12 code allows a maximum of two dwelling units on a qualifying lot. For this section, the code expressly recognizes two single-family dwelling units, one single-family dwelling + one ADU, or one duplex. That means a failed two-deed subdivision does not turn 1011 into an ordinary one-house lot.

LotScope Workbench proof-of-concept already passed on raw-land geometry

The earlier Workbench run tested a planning proxy equal to the reported 11,633 sf and found a viable two-detached-home topology: two 36' × 32' two-story plates, roughly 1,680 sf living target each, 22' × 22' integrated garages, modeled 10' building separation and direct B Street approaches. The deterministic search retained 80 passing coarse candidates and 100 passing refined candidates.

That was a raw-land / redevelopment test on proxy geometry, not a survey-based plan and not a retain-the-1911-house plan. Its value is strategic: if subdivision dies, the parcel still has a credible developer story that has survived a real geometry/circulation test.

Marketing fallback

If the front-30-ft BLA or short-plat path fails, market the property as a documented R-12 two-dwelling opportunity — with the survey, City response and LotScope test attached — instead of reverting to a generic “large yard” listing.

Open current R-12 two-unit rule

6. Demolition and ADU rules create timing options — not reasons to spend money now

1911 demolition gate

Any CDA building originally constructed before 1960 is subject to the City's historic-demolition review process before the demolition permit can issue. The code says the process does not permanently deny demolition, but it adds review, documentation and possible Commission involvement.

For you, teardown remains a developer/buyer decision unless the existing house itself becomes a sale blocker.

Open demolition-review code

ADU law is changing

Current codified CDA ADU rules still show an 800-sf maximum, no more than 75% of the primary dwelling, one extra parking space and no separate subdivision of the ADU. City staff stated that Idaho SB 1354 requires CDA to revise its ADU rules by February 1, 2027; staff specifically discussed a 1,000-sf allowance and related parking/height changes.

That is future upside if you still own the parcel then. It is not a reason to delay a needed exit or design to rules that are not yet codified.

Current ADU code · 2026 City discussion

7. Airbnb / short-term income is useful runway — but keep it clean

CDA currently requires a short-term-rental permit before offering a dwelling for stays of 30 days or fewer, subject to a narrow exception for no more than 14 rental days per calendar year divided into no more than two stays. The permit is non-transferable and automatically expires when title transfers.

Because short-term income is helping you carry the mortgage, confirm the current operating setup is compliant and preserve booking/income/depreciation records for the CPA. This is both a sale-risk issue and a tax issue.

Open STR permit rule

Your rule

Use roommates / Airbnb as a bridge to the next decision gate, not as a reason to keep an unaffordable property indefinitely.

8. Gift tax and the paid fallback

If 1007 gifts the strip

The federal annual gift-tax exclusion is $19,000 per donee for 2026. A gift above the annual exclusion can create a Form 709 reporting requirement for the donor even when no immediate gift tax is payable because of the lifetime exclusion. The tiny strip's ordinary dirt value may be below that threshold, but its assemblage value is unusual enough that nobody should invent a value.

1007 gets its own CPA/attorney. 1011 keeps the deed, survey, value support and basis records.

IRS gift-tax FAQ

If “gift” is declined — client authority card

First move: ask 1007 to name the number. Do not bid against ourselves.

Forced first anchor: prior owner-side planning used about $2,500.

Same-call ceiling: about $5,000 only if you have expressly decided that limit in advance. Anything above that ceiling should stop the conversation until you decide privately.

If price or other consideration is agreed, the transaction stops being documented as a gift. Convert the LOI/agreement/deed into a paid BLA conveyance through title/Idaho counsel. Any deferred-payment or closing-credit structure also needs separate your authorization and written documentation.

Same-call continuation after a “no” to the gift:
“I understand. If a gift doesn't work for you, is there a number that would make the small front piece worth doing, assuming the survey and City confirm it doesn't hurt your property?”

9. Data traps we are deliberately excluding

GIS dimensions ≠ survey

A visible map label, blue parcel outline or aerial scale can be off by feet. None may establish a wall setback or legal frontage.

Consumer assessment data conflict

Portal tax/assessment values disagree. Use Kootenai County's assessor record for assessed value; use a broker/appraiser for market value.

Wrong-property drift

An older archived “Midtown” investor package containing 93-foot frontage / foreclosure facts was explicitly rejected in the consolidated AV work because it did not match 1011. Do not let those facts re-enter this file.

Bottom line: the biggest remaining risks are not zoning density. They are exact boundary geometry, the original plat/2012 instrument, house/garage setbacks, legal alley/access, utility independence, lender releases and City acceptance of the jogged future lot. Close those cheaply; do not spend your scarce cash solving construction problems a buyer can solve later.

To: Owner(s) of 1007 N B St, Coeur d’Alene, Idaho (“1007 Owner”)

No purchase price for the land is proposed.

Nothing moves unless a licensed surveyor and the City confirm the adjustment can be done lawfully.

The final line will be designed to avoid creating a new setback, access, utility, easement, or title problem for 1007.

The gift area will be described by the surveyor, not by this letter or a GIS screenshot.

Any lender or title-company consent required for 1007 must be obtained before recording.

1007 is encouraged to use its own attorney, CPA, surveyor, lender, or title advisor. AeroVista and anyone assisting 1011 represent only 1011.

If the survey or City review shows the concept would materially harm 1007, the parties may stop without completing the gift.

Process costs. The 1011 Owner intends to arrange the survey/title/City/recording work needed for the proposed adjustment, subject to the 1011 Owner’s written budget approval. This is not a promise to pay any purchase price for the land or any separate compensation.

Except for permission to coordinate survey access if checked below and the parties’ agreement not to misrepresent this proposal to third parties, this letter is a statement of intent only. Document B — Conditional Boundary Line Adjustment & Gift Agreement

OWNER-SIDE WORKING DRAFT — attorney/title review required before signature.

1. Parties and property. This Conditional Boundary Line Adjustment & Gift Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered as of ____________, 2026, by and between ______________________________, owner(s) of 1007 N B St, Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, APN C3510003003A (“Grantor”), and ______________________________, owner(s) of 1011 N B St, Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, APN C3510003001A (“Grantee”). Grantee and all advisors engaged by Grantee represent only Grantee. Grantor is not represented by Grantee or AeroVista and is encouraged to obtain independent legal, tax, lender, title, and surveying advice.

2. Gift; no purchase price. Grantor agrees, subject to every condition in this Agreement, to convey the Transfer Area to Grantee as a voluntary gift and without a purchase price. The parties intend the land conveyance itself to be a gift. Grantee may pay approved third-party expenses of surveying, title, City processing, lender-release processing, escrow, and recording, but those payments are not a negotiated purchase price for the Transfer Area. No cash consideration for the land is due unless a later written amendment is separately approved and signed by Grantee.

3. Concept Transfer Area. The “Transfer Area” means only the area established by an Idaho licensed surveyor and approved through the City of Coeur d’Alene boundary-line-adjustment process. The design objective is approximately one (1) foot of southward boundary movement at the B Street frontage for approximately thirty (30) feet of depth, followed by a return to the existing common boundary before the garage/setback area. The final metes-and-bounds legal description attached as Exhibit A controls over every estimate, sketch, GIS line, or narrative.

4. Conditions precedent. Grantee has no obligation to complete or accept the transfer unless, in Grantee’s reasonable judgment: (a) the survey establishes the desired frontage benefit at 1011; (b) the City approves the BLA; (c) the adjustment does not create an unlawful structure setback, access, utility, easement, or parcel condition at 1007 or 1011; (d) current title reports are acceptable to Grantee; (e) any required mortgage/deed-of-trust holder consent or partial release is obtained; (f) the City/Planning or Engineering response does not materially defeat the intended future two-lot feasibility at 1011; and (g) total third-party costs remain within a budget separately approved in writing by Grantee.

5. Survey and City process. Grantor authorizes reasonable, pre-scheduled access for Grantee’s licensed surveyor and other professionals to observe and measure the common boundary and nearby improvements. Grantee may prepare and submit the BLA application and supporting materials. Grantor will reasonably cooperate by signing owner authorizations and City/title documents necessary to process the BLA, provided no document imposes a monetary obligation on Grantor without Grantor’s separate written consent.

6. Title and lender cooperation. Grantor will provide information reasonably needed to obtain a current title report. Grantor will not knowingly create a new lien or convey the Transfer Area to another party after signing this Agreement. If a lender or lienholder must release the Transfer Area, completion is contingent upon that written release. Grantee is not liable if a lender, title company, City, or other authority refuses approval.

7. Deed and recording. After all conditions are satisfied or waived by Grantee in writing, Grantor shall execute a Gift Warranty Deed conveying the Transfer Area to Grantee. The deed shall contain the surveyor’s metes-and-bounds description and shall be recorded with Kootenai County in the sequence required by the City/title company, together with or in coordination with the approved Record of Survey. No GIS image or conceptual exhibit may be recorded as the legal description.

8. Taxes and independent advice. Each party is responsible for that party’s own federal/state tax reporting and professional advice. No party makes a representation that the gift is exempt from gift-tax reporting, that no Form 709 is required, or that any particular basis treatment applies. Grantor acknowledges the opportunity to obtain independent tax advice before deed execution.

9. No promise of subdivision or value. Grantor is not asked to warrant that 1011 can later be subdivided, and Grantee makes no representation to Grantor regarding the future value or development outcome of 1011. The purpose of the transaction is the boundary adjustment itself. Grantee may pursue, abandon, sell, assign, develop, or otherwise use 1011 after closing as permitted by law.

10. Grantee termination right. Until the Gift Warranty Deed is recorded, Grantee may terminate this Agreement by written notice if any condition precedent is not satisfied, if the proposed adjustment no longer advances Grantee’s objectives, or if Grantee determines that the cost/timing is inconsistent with the 1011 owner’s financial needs. Upon termination, neither party is required to convey the Transfer Area; accrued third-party invoices remain the responsibility of the party that ordered them unless otherwise agreed in writing.

11. Assignment by Grantee. Grantee may assign this Agreement, without additional consideration to Grantor, to a purchaser or successor in title to 1011, to a revocable trust or entity controlled by Grantee, or to an escrow/title company solely to complete the transaction, by written notice to Grantor. No assignment releases the original Grantee from an obligation already due unless Grantor agrees in writing.

12. No brokers; no commission. Each party represents that it has not engaged a broker in connection with this small boundary gift whose compensation would be owed by the other party. Grantee will not be responsible for a brokerage commission claimed through Grantor.

13. Entire agreement; amendments. This Agreement and its exhibits contain the complete agreement concerning the proposed gift/BLA and supersede prior oral discussions on that subject. Any amendment must be written and signed by both parties, except that Grantee may approve or reject survey/City/title conditions as expressly stated above.

14. Governing law; venue. This Agreement is intended to be governed by Idaho law. Venue for any dispute shall be in Kootenai County, Idaho, unless the parties later agree otherwise in writing. This clause should be reviewed by Idaho counsel before execution.

15. Counterparts and electronic signatures. The parties may sign counterparts and electronic copies to the extent accepted by the professionals processing the transaction. The final deed and any instrument requiring notarization shall be signed and acknowledged in the form required for recording.

Document F — Owner-Side Negotiation Rules & Call Script

Rule 1 — Gift first The first ask is a gift. There is no standing authority to offer $1, $10, $10,000, or any other land price. If 1007 asks for money, say you need to take it back to the 1011 owner.
Rule 2 — Do not disclose distress Do not tell 1007 that the owner is broke, desperate, under time pressure, or has a specific minimum sale price. That information weakens the owner and is not needed to make the boundary correction.
Rule 3 — Be truthful about purpose You may say the owner is trying to clarify and improve the parcel’s frontage and potential future options. Do not falsely say the adjustment has no value or cannot affect development. Do not promise subdivision approval.
Rule 4 — Protect the friendship The concept should stop before the garage and be conditioned on a survey showing no new nonconformity. Invite 1007 to use its own advisor. A clean gift between friends is more durable when neither side feels rushed or misled.

Suggested opening call/text:

“Hey — we found an old county note showing a one-foot piece from 1011 was combined into your parcel back in 2012. We’re trying to clean up the old frontage, and it looks like we may only need the front ~30 feet of that one-foot strip — not anything near your garage. Would you be open to gifting that tiny piece back if a licensed survey and the City confirm it doesn’t create a problem for your property? We can put the line right back where it is now before the garage. No pressure; I just wanted to ask you first before spending money on the survey.”

If they ask, “What’s it worth to you?”

“We’re starting by asking if you’d be willing to gift it because it’s such a tiny piece and appears connected to an old lot-line change. I don’t have authority to offer a purchase price. If a gift doesn’t work for you, I can take that back to the owner before we go any further.”

If they ask whether it helps subdivision:

“It may help our frontage, but we don’t have City approval and we’re not representing that it creates a second legal lot. That’s exactly what the survey and City review are for.”

Final use warning

These are owner-side working drafts, not legal forms guaranteed to be enforceable or recordable. Idaho counsel/title should finalize Document B and Document D. The City’s BLA code requires a warranty deed, a licensed survey, compliance of resulting lots, and recording coordination. The legal description is intentionally blank until the surveyor prepares it. 1007 should have independent counsel/tax advice.

Conditional Boundary Gift & Active-Sale Cooperation Agreement

Effective Date: ____________________, 2026, at ________ ☐ a.m. ☐ p.m.

Grantor / 1007 Owner(s): ______________________________________________________________

Grantee / 1011 Owner(s): ______________________________________________________________

1. Parties, Parent Parcels, and Working Record Description

This Conditional Boundary Gift & Active-Sale Cooperation Agreement (“Agreement”) is between the owner(s) of 1007 N B St, Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, APN C3510003003A (“Grantor”), and the owner(s) of 1011 N B St, Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, APN C3510003001A (“Grantee”).

For working-reference purposes only, public-record research identifies the 1011 parcel as FOREST HEIGHTS, LT 1, LT 2 EX S 1 FT BLK 3 1450N04W and identifies the 1007 parcel as including S 1 FT OF LT 2, LT 3, N2 OF LT 4, BLOCK 3. These are not substituted for the current title company legal descriptions.

AeroVista and persons assisting Grantee act only for Grantee. Grantor is not represented by AeroVista or Grantee and is encouraged to obtain independent legal, tax, title, lender, brokerage, and surveying advice.

2. Background and Intended Boundary Area

The parties understand that historical parcel information suggests a one-foot portion of original Lot 2 is presently included with the 1007 parcel. The parties wish to investigate a small boundary line adjustment that may return only a front portion of that area to 1011.

The intended area (“Concept Transfer Area”) is approximately one (1.00) foot of southward boundary movement at the B Street frontage for approximately thirty (30) feet of lot depth, followed by a return to the existing common boundary before the 1007 garage/setback area. The exact shape, dimensions, bearings, area, and legal description will be established only by an Idaho licensed surveyor and City approval.

The parties agree that any conceptual sketch, GIS image, aerial image, or narrative is explanatory only and is not a recordable legal description.

3. Gift Intent; No Purchase Price for Land

Subject to this Agreement’s conditions, Grantor states the present intent to convey the final City-approved Transfer Area to Grantee as a voluntary gift and without a purchase price for the land.

Grantee may pay approved third-party costs associated with survey, title, City processing, lender-release processing, escrow, recording, or related diligence. Those process-cost payments are not intended by the parties to be a negotiated purchase price for the land.

If the parties later agree to money or other consideration for the land itself, that change must be documented in a separate written amendment reviewed by title/Idaho counsel. The transaction will no longer be treated as a pure gift merely because this Agreement began that way.

4. Immediate Cooperation and Survey Access

Beginning on the Effective Date, Grantor authorizes reasonable, pre-scheduled exterior access by Grantee’s licensed surveyor and field crew to locate the common boundary, property corners, structures near the line, walls/eaves, fences, driveways, visible utilities/service features, and other items reasonably necessary to evaluate the proposed boundary line adjustment.

Grantor agrees to reasonably cooperate with title, survey, City, and lender inquiries and to sign owner authorizations reasonably necessary to process the proposed boundary line adjustment, provided no document imposes an unapproved monetary obligation on Grantor.

Grantee will use commercially reasonable efforts to order the preliminary survey and title work promptly after signature and to avoid unnecessary interference with the marketing or use of 1007.

5. Conditions Before Final Conveyance

No final conveyance is required unless all of the following conditions are satisfied or expressly waived in writing by Grantee where legally permissible:

A licensed survey establishes a Transfer Area acceptable to Grantee and shows the intended frontage benefit at 1011.

The proposed adjustment does not create a new unlawful setback, encroachment, access, utility, easement, or parcel condition at 1007 or 1011.

The City of Coeur d’Alene approves the boundary line adjustment and the required Record of Survey.

Current title reports are acceptable to Grantee and confirm a lawful conveyance path.

Any required deed-of-trust holder, mortgage lender, lienholder, or other secured party gives the required consent or partial release.

The City/Planning/Engineering response does not materially defeat the owner’s intended frontage/subdivision feasibility objective at 1011.

Total third-party costs remain within the Grantee’s separately approved budget.

If a condition fails, the parties may redesign the proposed line, extend the diligence period by written agreement, or terminate this Agreement without completing the land transfer, subject to Section 9 regarding reliance costs.

6. Active Listing; Protection Against an Intervening Sale

The parties acknowledge that, as of the Effective Date, the 1007 property is: ☐ actively listed for sale ☐ under contract ☐ not listed ☐ other: _______________________________.

Grantor may continue marketing 1007 and is not required by this Agreement to reject a bona fide purchase offer. However, Grantor agrees that the pending boundary-adjustment process will be handled openly enough to avoid an intervening sale unintentionally defeating the parties’ signed agreement.

Grantor will promptly provide a copy or written notice of this Agreement to Grantor’s listing broker/agent and authorizes Grantee, Grantee’s surveyor, and the selected title/escrow company to communicate with the listing broker/agent solely as reasonably necessary to coordinate the proposed boundary adjustment.

If Grantor accepts an offer to sell 1007 before the boundary adjustment records, Grantor will notify Grantee in writing within one (1) business day after acceptance, including the expected closing date if known.

Before any such closing, Grantor will use commercially reasonable efforts to accomplish one of the following: (a) complete the approved boundary adjustment and conveyance before the 1007 closing; or (b) obtain a written assumption/cooperation agreement from the buyer substantially in the form of Exhibit D, so the buyer succeeds to Grantor’s cooperation obligations after closing.

Grantor will not knowingly instruct an escrow/title company to close a sale of 1007 in a manner that intentionally defeats this Agreement without first giving Grantee prompt written notice and a reasonable opportunity to coordinate either pre-closing completion or buyer assumption, subject to the actual buyer, lender, title, and City requirements.

GRANTOR INITIALS — ACTIVE SALE SECTION: ____________ GRANTEE INITIALS: ____________

7. Diligence Period and Long-Stop Date

The initial diligence period is fifteen (15) business days after the Effective Date. During that period Grantee will use reasonable efforts to obtain a preliminary survey/BLA exhibit, title information, and an initial City/Engineering or Planning response.

If those items are actively in process but not completed because of surveyor, City, title, or lender timing outside Grantee’s reasonable control, the diligence period automatically extends once for fifteen (15) additional calendar days unless Grantor gives written notice that a bona fide sale closing requires a shorter coordination period.

Unless extended in writing, this Agreement terminates forty-five (45) calendar days after the Effective Date if the BLA has not been approved or placed into a closing/recording process. The parties may shorten or extend that date in writing.

8. Process Costs and No Open-Ended Commitment

Grantee will arrange and pay only those third-party survey, title, City, escrow, recording, and lender-release processing costs that Grantee separately approves. Grantor is not required to pay Grantee’s professional costs unless Section 9 applies.

Grantor remains responsible for Grantor’s own attorney, CPA, broker, tax, and independent advisor costs unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Nothing in this Agreement authorizes a land purchase price, brokerage commission, or open-ended development expense.

9. Reliance Costs if Grantor Voluntarily Defeats the Process

The parties recognize that Grantee may spend money in reliance on Grantor’s signed cooperation. If Grantor later voluntarily withdraws solely for convenience, or voluntarily closes a sale of 1007 before the Long-Stop Date without either completing the BLA or obtaining buyer assumption, and no survey/City/title/lender/no-harm condition has failed, then the parties elect ONE of the following:

☐ OPTION A — Neighbor-friendly Each side bears its own costs; no reimbursement.
☐ OPTION B — Protect 1011 reliance Grantor reimburses Grantee’s documented, nonrefundable third-party survey/title/City costs actually incurred after signature, capped at $____________.

No reimbursement is owed if the proposed adjustment fails because of survey geometry, City refusal, title/lender requirements, a material adverse effect on 1007, or Grantee’s own decision not to proceed.

10. Final Survey, City Approval, Warranty Deed, and Recording

This Agreement does not presently transfer title to any land. After all required conditions are satisfied, the licensed surveyor will prepare the final Record of Survey and metes-and-bounds legal description, and Grantor will execute the final warranty deed required for the approved boundary line adjustment.

No party will sign or record a deed containing a blank, guessed, GIS-derived, or merely conceptual legal description. The future deed’s Exhibit A must be the final surveyor-prepared description accepted by the City/title company.

The title/escrow company will coordinate the recording sequence for the warranty deed and Record of Survey and will confirm any required lender releases or consents before recording.

The parties understand that the BLA itself does not create a second legal lot at 1011; any future subdivision is a separate City/county process.

11. No Promise of Future Subdivision, Value, or Tax Result

Grantor does not warrant that 1011 can later be subdivided, and Grantee makes no promise to Grantor concerning future development or value at 1011.

Neither party represents that the gift has any particular tax treatment, fair market value, basis result, or reporting outcome. Grantor is encouraged to obtain independent tax advice before the final deed is executed.

The parties agree not to state to third parties that two legal lots have been created unless and until the applicable subdivision process has actually been completed and recorded.

12. Listing Broker, Prospective Buyer, Title, and Lender Communications

Grantor authorizes limited disclosure of this Agreement and related survey/BLA materials to Grantor’s listing broker, a bona fide prospective buyer or buyer’s representative, the parties’ title/escrow companies, lenders/lienholders, surveyor, City staff, and attorneys/CPAs solely as reasonably necessary to process, evaluate, assume, or close the boundary adjustment.

No such disclosure creates an agency relationship with Grantee or AeroVista, and no listing broker or buyer becomes a party unless that person separately signs a written assumption or agreement.

13. No Recording of This Agreement; No Standalone Parcel

Neither party will record this Agreement or a memorandum of it against 1007 or 1011 without a separate written agreement and Idaho counsel/title approval. The purpose of this clause is to avoid an unintended title cloud while the City BLA is being processed.

No document will be recorded that purports to create a standalone approximately 30-square-foot parcel. The eventual deed must operate only as part of the approved boundary adjustment and merger into 1011.

14. Authority, Entire Agreement, Amendment, Assignment, and Governing Law

Each signer represents that the signer is an owner of the parcel identified for that party or has written authority to bind that owner. If additional co-owners, spouses, entities, trustees, or other vested parties are required, this Agreement and the final deed remain subject to obtaining their signatures.

This Agreement, including its exhibits, contains the parties’ current agreement concerning the proposed gift/BLA and supersedes prior oral discussions on that subject. Any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties.

Grantee may assign this Agreement to a purchaser or successor in title to 1011, a revocable trust or entity controlled by Grantee, or an escrow/title company solely to facilitate completion, by written notice to Grantor. Grantor may not assign the cooperation obligations except through a written buyer assumption consistent with Exhibit D.

This Agreement is intended to be governed by Idaho law, with venue in Kootenai County, Idaho. Idaho counsel should review this provision and the Agreement before the parties rely on it as a final real-property contract.

15. Counterparts, Electronic Copies, and Optional Notarization

The parties may sign counterparts and exchange scanned/electronic copies. The parties intend signatures on this Agreement to evidence the agreement and cooperation described here.

Optional notarization may be used on the same day to authenticate signatures. Notarization of this Agreement does not substitute for the later survey-backed warranty deed and does not itself transfer the Transfer Area.

Drafting Notes & Legal/Process References (Not Part of the Agreement)

The existing AeroVista transaction package already conditions any final gift on survey, City approval, title, no new nonconformity, and lender/partial-release requirements.

Coeur d’Alene’s BLA application requires an Idaho licensed surveyor and a Record of Survey. City materials state that building permits will not issue on adjusted parcels until the BLA requirements are met and the Record of Survey and warranty deeds are recorded.

Idaho’s statute of frauds requires agreements for the sale of real property or an interest in it to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged. Idaho law also requires transfers of interests in real property to be in writing.

Idaho recording law generally requires acknowledgment before an instrument may be recorded. This is why the future warranty deed, not this same-day cooperation agreement, is the critical recordable conveyance instrument.

Idaho case law also emphasizes that a real-property contract must identify the property sufficiently. Because the exact 1-foot × ~30-foot area has not yet been surveyed, this draft deliberately avoids pretending the conceptual area is a final recordable legal description.

Owner-side caution.This document is designed to capture consent and cooperation quickly, not to replace an Idaho attorney, title company, surveyor, lender release, City approval, or the final deed. If the parties want a document intended for specific performance or other strong real-property remedies before a survey legal description exists, Idaho counsel should revise it before signature.

Set your limits before the conversation

These fields are for you only and stay in this browser. The earlier $2,500 / $5,000 figures are planning references, not standing authority.

Enter your limits before the conversation. If you have not pre-authorized a number, the correct live answer is “I need to think about it.”
When price is agreed: capture the exact number in the paid term sheet, but normally do not hand over money that day. Move payment through title/escrow when the approved BLA, lender releases, deed and Record of Survey can close together.
This page is your paid fallback only. Start with the gift. Do not introduce money unless 1007 declines the gift or says a gift is not workable. Before the conversation, decide your private same-call authority. If you have not pre-authorized a number, do not invent one under pressure.

Your rules before you call

Protect your urgency

Do not tell 1007 you are broke, desperate, behind, under a forced-sale deadline, or carrying a specific mortgage balance. You can truthfully say you are trying to clean up the parcel frontage and preserve your future options.

Gift first

The first ask is still a gift of the small front area, subject to survey, City, title, lender, and no-harm conditions.

Never bid against yourself

If the gift is declined, ask 1007 what number would make the small front piece worth doing. Let them anchor first whenever possible.

Same-call script after “no” to the gift

You:
“I understand. If a gift doesn’t work for you, is there a number that would make the small front piece worth doing, assuming the survey and City confirm it doesn’t hurt your property?”

If they say: “You make me an offer.”

If you have expressly pre-authorized the earlier planning anchor, you may use approximately $2,500. If you have not authorized it, say you need to think about it and call them back.

“I was hoping to keep this very simple because it’s such a small piece and we’re paying the survey/title/City costs. I could consider $2,500, subject to the survey, City, title and lender pieces all working. I don’t want to promise more than I’ve decided I can do.”

If they say: “$5,000.”

If — and only if — you privately decided before the conversation that $5,000 is within your same-call authority, you can conditionally accept. Keep every survey/City/title/no-harm/lender condition.

“If the survey and City confirm the front-only adjustment works and doesn’t create a problem for your place, I can work with $5,000. We’d still have title and any lender approval to clear, and we’d put the paid version in writing.”

If they say: “$10,000” or “$15,000.”

“That’s more than I’m prepared to agree to on the spot. Let me look at the total survey, City and title cost and I’ll get back to you. I don’t want to say yes to a number I haven’t actually worked through.”

Do not negotiate against yourself by instantly countering upward. Write down the number and leave the call cleanly.

If they ask: “What is it really worth to you?”

“We don’t know yet. We still need a licensed survey and a City answer, so I’m not treating subdivision or a particular value increase as guaranteed. What I know today is that the small front adjustment may improve the frontage, and I’m trying to see whether there’s a simple deal that works for both of us.”

If they say: “You’re going to make a lot of money on this.”

“Maybe it improves the property, but there are still survey, City, title, lender and subdivision steps and no guarantee of the outcome. I’m paying to find that out. I’m trying to price the small boundary piece fairly without pretending the future is already approved.”

If they are worried about the garage or value of 1007

“That’s exactly why I only want the front portion and why the agreement stops if the survey shows the line creates a problem for your garage, access, utilities or property. I don’t want to make your lot worse.”

If they say they are selling and do not want complications

“I understand. That’s why I’d like to move quickly and keep it small. If we can get the cooperation signed now, we can order the survey/title work immediately and coordinate with your listing agent and title company. If the BLA can’t be completed before your sale, an incoming buyer can decide whether to assume the cooperation in writing.”

If they refuse outright

“Understood. I appreciate you hearing me out. I’m not going to pressure you. If you change your mind before the property sells, let me know.”

Your authority card

DecisionYour private answer before the call
GiftAlways the first ask.
First cash anchor if forcedEarlier planning reference: about $2,500 — use only if you authorize it.
Same-call maximumEarlier planning reference: about $5,000 — use only if you expressly authorize it before the call.
Anything above your ceilingStop. Write the number down. Do not counter live. Re-run the economics first.
Money is agreedStop using the gift documents as the operative conveyance. Title/Idaho counsel converts the deal to a paid BLA conveyance.

Cash-constrained structures to discuss only after professional review

  • Payment at BLA/deed recording rather than at the verbal agreement.
  • Payment through title/escrow after City approval and lender release.
  • Payment tied to your eventual refinance or property closing if 1007 accepts that timing.
  • A modest deposit only if your attorney/title company says it is appropriate and the conditions are clearly refundable/nonrefundable in writing.

Do not casually promise a later payment, closing credit, profit share, or side deal. Any consideration changes the legal/tax documentation and needs to appear in the written paid agreement.

After-call record

Follow-up text if they stated a number but you did not agree

“Thanks for talking this through with me. I wrote down your $_____ number for the small front boundary area. I did not agree to it yet; I’m going to look at the survey/City/title costs and get back to you. Any deal would still be subject to the survey, City approval, title/lender requirements and no new problem for your property.”

Follow-up text if you conditionally agreed within authority

“Thanks — just confirming our conversation: we’re at $_____ for the small front boundary area, subject to a licensed survey, City BLA approval, title/lender clearance and the adjustment not creating a problem for 1007. We’ll have the paid version of the agreement documented properly before anything transfers.”

If the proposed line creates a material setback, garage, access, utility, easement, lender, title, or City issue, the parties may revise the line by written agreement so long as the revised area remains acceptable to Buyer and Seller and is approved by the surveyor/City/title. After all required conditions are satisfied or waived where legally permitted, Seller will execute the final warranty deed conveying the approved Transfer Area to Buyer. The deed must contain the licensed surveyor's final metes-and-bounds description.

Document H — Negotiation Assistance: Gift → Paid Fallback

YOUR JOB IS TO GET A CLEAN AGREEMENT, NOT TO WIN AN ARGUMENT

Before the conversation

  • Decide your true cash ceiling before you walk over. Your economic ceiling and your same-call cash ceiling can be different.
  • Have the gift packet and paid term sheet both ready. Do not switch a gift document into a paid deal by handwriting money into it.
  • Know your BATNA: if 1007 says no, you still have the one-parcel/two-dwelling R-12 fallback and can sell the documented upside. That keeps you from overpaying.
  • Keep your mortgage pressure, deadline, and expected upside private. Be truthful about the purpose: frontage and future options.
  • Plan to use title/escrow for any purchase price. Do not bring cash as a persuasion tool.

The live conversation tree

Situation Your move
Gift yes Confirm the yes out loud, sign the gift cooperation/survey access while together, optionally notarize, scan copies, notify listing side, order survey/title immediately.
Gift no, but open to money Say: “I understand. If a gift doesn’t work, what number would make the small front piece worth doing, assuming the survey and City show it doesn’t hurt your property?” Then stop talking.
They make a reasonable number inside your pre-set authority Repeat the exact number and conditions. Use the paid term sheet. Do not use the gift agreement/deed.
They say a number above your ceiling Do not counter against yourself. Say you need to evaluate the total survey/title/City cost and will get back to them.
They ask you to name the first number Only use a number you approved in advance. Prior planning used about $2,500 as a low anchor and about $5,000 as a same-call ceiling, but those are planning references, not standing authority.
They demand money today Say the price will be paid through title/escrow when the BLA can actually close. Do not hand over cash.
They ask for future profit / a percentage Prefer a fixed price. Do not agree to profit sharing on the spot; that creates a much more complicated agreement and tax/accounting problem.
They are worried about the listed sale Offer the short diligence window, broker notice, and buyer-assumption path. The goal is coordination, not freezing their sale.

Scripts that protect your position

After gift decline

“I understand. If a gift doesn’t work for you, is there a number that would make the small front piece worth doing, assuming the survey and City confirm it doesn’t hurt your property?”

If they ask what it is worth to you

“We don’t know yet. We still need the survey and a City answer. I’m not treating subdivision or a specific value increase as approved. I’m trying to see whether there’s a simple fixed-price deal that works for both of us.”

If they say you will make money

“It may improve the property, but there are still survey, City, title, lender and subdivision steps and no guaranteed outcome. I’m paying to find that out. I’d rather agree on a simple fixed price for the small boundary piece.”

If they ask for cash now

“I’m comfortable documenting the price today, but I want the money to go through title when the survey, City and lender pieces are cleared so neither of us gets stuck in a half-finished transaction.”

If they want $10k–$15k or more

“That’s more than I’m prepared to agree to on the spot. Let me look at the total cost and what the survey/City work still has to prove, and I’ll get back to you.”

If they say selling 1007 makes this too hard

“I understand. I’m not asking you to stop selling. I’m asking for a short cooperation window so we can rush the survey/title work, and if a buyer arrives first we can either finish before closing or let the buyer decide whether to assume it in writing.”

Private authority card

Gift request $0 — always first
If they force you to anchor Your approved number: $________________
Same-call maximum $________________
Absolute economic ceiling after full analysis $________________
Anything above same-call maximum Pause. No counter. Re-run economics.
Money agreed Use paid packet; title/escrow at recording.

Title/escrow: “I have a signed conditional paid BLA agreement. Please open title on both parcels, confirm vesting/liens/deeds of trust, identify any partial release needed, and tell me what you need to close the paid boundary conveyance through escrow after City approval.”

Process Notes & Sources (Not Part of the Agreement)

  • Coeur d'Alene's BLA application states that a Record of Survey completed by an Idaho licensed surveyor is required when property is manipulated for a lot-line adjustment and that building permits will not be issued until BLA requirements are met and the Record of Survey and warranty deeds are recorded.
  • Idaho Code § 9-505 requires an agreement for the sale of real property or an interest therein to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged.
  • Idaho Code § 55-601 provides that a conveyance of an estate in real property may be made by a written instrument subscribed by the party disposing of it and requires the grantee's name and complete mailing address on the instrument.
  • Idaho Code § 55-805 generally requires acknowledgment before an instrument may be recorded.
  • Because the exact Transfer Area is not yet surveyed, Idaho counsel/title should review whether the concept description plus the parent parcels is sufficient for the remedies the parties intend before anyone relies on the paid contract as a final enforceable land-sale agreement.

Owner-side legal caution.This packet deliberately avoids claiming that the same-day term sheet guarantees specific performance or a completed sale. The safer goal is to document the exact price and cooperation immediately, then move the licensed survey/title/City work fast and have Idaho counsel/title finalize the binding property description and closing documents.

AEROVISTA / LOTSCOPE • FINAL CONSOLIDATED PROPERTY STRATEGY

1011 N B Street

Coeur d’Alene, Idaho 83814 • APN C3510003001A

AV DECISION: ADVANCE THE FRONT-30-FT BOUNDARY GIFT FEASIBILITY — THEN SELL THE PROVEN UPSIDE

Prepared solely for the owner of 1011 N B St. This is not a survey, appraisal, title opinion, legal opinion, or city approval.

Executive conclusion The strongest low-cash strategy is no longer “build more.” It is to prove whether a very small boundary-line gift from 1007 — approximately 1 foot south along the B Street frontage for only the first 30 feet of depth, then returning to the existing common line before the garage — can restore roughly 100 feet of recognized frontage at 1011. If survey and City review confirm it, the owner may be able to convert a difficult ~99-foot frontage condition into a credible two-lot story without buying a full-depth strip or disturbing the neighbor’s garage-side setback. Because the owner needs a fast exit, AeroVista recommends proving this entitlement cheaply, documenting it, and monetizing the certainty rather than funding construction.

1. Owner mandate and transaction posture

This report consolidates the property work across the prior 1011 N B Street threads, the uploaded public-record review, the user-supplied GIS/aerial images, current Coeur d’Alene code, current market listings, and the later discovery involving 1007 N B Street. The transaction mandate is intentionally one-sided: AeroVista is working for the financially constrained owner of 1011 only.

Represent and protect the 1011 owner only. Do not describe AeroVista as representing 1007, the 1007 seller, or both sides.

Friend-first negotiation: the opening request is a gift of the small boundary area, not a purchase offer.

Do not volunteer the 1011 owner’s financial urgency, projected subdivision profit, or internal walk-away economics. Do not make any false statement if directly asked.

No cash offer for the land should be made without the 1011 owner’s separate written authorization.

The owner should avoid construction, demolition, or expensive design work until frontage, title, setbacks, access, and City interpretation are proven.

1007 should be expressly encouraged to obtain its own attorney, tax advisor, title advice, and lender consent. This preserves both the friendship and the enforceability of a clean transaction.

2. Current property fact base

Existing home Approx. 1,320 sf; 3 bed / 2 bath; built 1911 High
